newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Statoil to focus on core areas.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Statoil to focus on core areas.

text.p: A programme of buying, selling and swapping acreage off Norway has been instigated by Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) as part of plans to focus on core areas of the shelf, the company Status Weekly magazine said on Thursday.

"Our primary approach will be to discover and develop oil and gas resources through to the production phase in acreage awarded by offshore licensing rounds," executive vice president Johan Nic Vold was quoted as saying.
He said core areas were those where Statoil already had an interest in production fields or in which a basis existed for future production.
"Strengthening our holdings in projects that can help to achieve and maintain our long-term production profile will be particularly important," Vold said.
He said Statoil's operations would focus on the Sleipner, quadrant 25 (north of Sleipner), Tampenkilen (Snorre/Visund/Statfjord/Gullfaks), the Oseberg and Troll areas of the North Sea.
Similarily, Statoil will concentrate on the Aasgard/Heidrun/Norne area outside mid-Norway and the Tromsoe patch off northern Norway, he said.

Statoil is also making efforts to qualify new core areas through exploration and by following up proven resources in the Barents Sea, the southern part of Norway's North Sea sector and the deepwater areas of the Norwegian Sea, Status Weekly said.
